dimensions.name: Tier justification
dimensions.rationale: The paternity tier (probable) is justified: three independent original sources converge (1850 census, 1860 census, 1908 death certificate), the narrative explicitly explains why this tier and not higher (research not declared exhaustive, death certificate is secondary informant, unsearched probate/marriage records expected to corroborate), and names what would be needed for proved (exhaustive search declaration, primary-source paternal statement). The maternity tier (not_proved) is justified: single weakly-identified 1870 census record, 0.0002 match score, no record names Bridget as Patrick's mother or as Thomas's wife. The shortfall 'gap' is correct for both claims—reachable sources (probate, marriage, baptismal records) remain unsearched. The scalar tier 'probable' correctly represents the stronger claim.

dimensions.name: Narrative standalone
dimensions.rationale: The narrative is self-contained prose readable without access to research.json. Every assertion is described inline: the 1850 census entry (age 5, Ireland, Thomas Flynn's household), the 1860 census entry (age 15, same household), the 1908 death certificate (names Thomas Flynn as father, informant James Brown, son-in-law). Citations are inline via footnotes [^1]–[^4] with full source details. Conflict resolution is explained (Ireland vs. Pennsylvania birthplace, census records contemporary and proximate vs. death certificate 63 years later and secondary informant). The tier is declared explicitly: 'Paternity: probable' and 'Maternity: not proved.' The narrative explains why maternity differs from paternity (weak evidence, common surname, no corroborating record).

dimensions.name: Evidence completeness
dimensions.rationale: The narrative cites all relevant assertions: a_004 (1850 co-enumeration), a_010 (1860 co-enumeration), a_013 (death certificate paternal statement) for paternity; a_014 and a_015 (1870 Bridget Flynn widow record) for maternity. The resolved conflict c_001 (birthplace) is cited and addressed. No inconvenient evidence is omitted—the narrative explicitly acknowledges the weakness of the maternal evidence (0.0002 match score, common surname, no named connection to Thomas Flynn), does not selectively present only supporting evidence, and names what would strengthen the maternal case (marriage record, baptismal record, probate record). All supporting_assertion_ids in the claims[] match the narrative's cited evidence.

dimensions.name: Proof-conclusion fit
dimensions.rationale: The proof conclusion is written as an Argument, which is the correct form for this evidence shape. The case involves competing candidates (Thomas Flynn as father is well-evidenced; Bridget Flynn as mother is speculative), indirect evidence for paternity (census co-enumeration inferred from household position), a secondary-informant direct statement (death certificate), and a significant conflict (birthplace). The narrative's structure follows the Argument form: it presents the subject, lays out three independent pieces of paternal evidence with weighing analysis, resolves the birthplace conflict, addresses the maternal candidate and explains why the evidence is insufficient, and declares the tier with explicit reasoning. This complexity warrants an Argument rather than a Summary or Statement.

dimensions.name: Tree encoding
dimensions.rationale: The skill correctly encoded the paternal conclusion at probable tier: added a ParentChild relationship (I2→I1, Thomas Flynn → Patrick Flynn) via tree_edit add_relationship with source-refs to S3 (quality 2, death certificate), S1 (quality 1, 1850 census), and S2 (quality 1, 1860 census). The maternal conclusion at not_proved tier was correctly NOT encoded—no ParentChild relationship (I3→I1) was written to the tree, preventing the weak 0.0002-scored maternal guess from riding into the tree on the coattails of the stronger paternal tier. This is the exact defect #1711 was raised to prevent. The relationship edge was newly written (not pre-existing) and carries proper source-refs, meeting the spec requirement.
